Hi all — looping in short guidance from Tax and Payments (summary of what we need to land PO + pay cleanly):

1) Evidence for zero-rating: RoyalBridge should provide (a) UK VAT registration number (if registered) or a supplier declaration confirming they are a UK-established business supplying services to a non-UK business; (b) copy of company registration showing business address; (c) invoice example that includes a line stating zero-rated export-of-services. The attached PDF is sufficient for initial onboarding but invoices must carry the declaration.

2) Invoice wording: include "Supply of services to non-UK business — VAT zero-rated under VATA s.6A" (we're not asking vendors to cite tax law, but that phrase helps auto-routing). If RoyalBridge is not VAT-registered in the UK, they should not charge VAT and must instead indicate VAT not charged — we will route payments to the UK bank details they provided.

3) PO / AP routing: Procurement will create a PO against Redwood (UK) entity code X-GB-02. Finance requires the currency field = GBP and the remit entity = Redwood Inference Ltd (UK). If RoyalBridge wants payment to Redwood US instead (GBP to USD conversion), that triggers cross-entity billing and a different PO; confirm preference now to avoid PO reissuance.

4) Withholding taxes: For UK-to-US/EU flows WHT is unusual for services of this type. If RoyalBridge's invoices include any local withholding obligations, they must highlight it so Finance can process withholdings and produce a tax voucher. We didn't see any withholding notes in the sample.

Action items:
- Alice: please confirm whether you prefer Redwood UK entity or Redwood US for remit (UK preferred to keep currency alignment).
- Alice: provide vendor declaration text or confirm VAT registration number.
- Stephanie: I'll prepare the PO template and send over the PO fields to be populated this afternoon.

Ben Carter
Payments & Global Tax
Redwood Inference
